question.text: Mr. Prakash Rao, a resident individual LP, has total income of INR 6 crore for FY25 — composed of INR 5.5 crore LTCG on unlisted equity via Cat II AIF pass-through and INR 50 lakh from salary. Under the Finance Act 2022 amendment, what is the MAXIMUM surcharge rate applicable on the LTCG component of his tax?

answer.text: 15% — maximum surcharge on income referred to in Section 111A/112/112A or dividend shall not exceed 15%

explanation.text: The Logic: Per workbook Para 16.3 / Finance Act 2022: where an individual's total income comprises income under Section 111A (STCG), 112/112A (LTCG) or dividend, the MAXIMUM surcharge on tax on SUCH income is capped at 15% — even though the non-capital-gains surcharge slab on INR 6 cr total income would otherwise be 37%. So on the LTCG tax @ 12.5% = 68.75 lakh, surcharge is capped at 15% = INR 10.3125 lakh. The 37% applies only to the salary-portion tax. The Trap: Option A ignores the 15% cap. Option B is the Section 115BAC new-regime cap on TOTAL income surcharge. Option D invents a flat rate. Cross-Exam Context: XXI-A (PMS Distributor) covers this for PMS income; XIX-C for AIF pass-through income. Manager's Pro-Tip: When advising HNW LPs, explicitly model the 15% surcharge cap in the net-return illustration — the difference between 37% and 15% surcharge on cap gains can move the IRR by 100+ bps. Distribute income tagged by 111A/112A head for Form 64C clarity.
